newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks set new highs.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks set new highs.

text.p: Stock market records were shattered Friday as fresh economic data pointing to moderating economic growth and tame inflation, heightened investor hopes that the Federal Reserve will leave interest rates unchanged.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 66.58 points or 1.15 percent, at a record 5,838.52, beating the old high of 5,778.00 set May 22. The Standard & Poor's composite index also set a new high.
For the week, the Dow jumped 178.66 points, the second biggest weekly point gain ever after the Aug. 2 week's 206.77-point surge.

"Mood, momentum and money flow are back in gear," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "This is the magic moment that people have talked so often about, the Dow has broken through 5,800 and now some have lifted their sights to 6,000."

Investors rushed the market, buying up stocks after the Labour Department reported that the Consumer Price Index inched up just 0.1 percent, confirming that inflation was still dormant. A day earlier, it said that the Producer Price Index edged up 0.3 percent in August.
In another report, retail sales rose a modest 0.2 percent, suggesting that consumers are not spending at a rate that would spur price increases.
"The data clearly suggests that the Fed does not need to raise interest rates at its upcoming Sept. 24 FOMC meeting," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,716 to 719 on heavy volume of 487 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index posted its seventh biggest point gain in history, jumping 22.86 to 1,188.67 on the strength in technology stocks, but still left it short of its record 1,249.15 set June 5.

"Goldilocks is back -- the economy is not too hot or too cold," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers. "This is the kind of environment where we'll have a Dow 6,000 by the election."
The Treasury bond market also rose, with the 30-year bond gaining 1-17/32, sending its yield below the psychologically important 7 percent level to 6.95 percent from 7.08 percent at Thursday's close.
"The buyers came and never left. A lot of people are piling on here now that we're in record territory," said Marty Kearney, a trader at PTI Securities.
William LeFevre, senior market analyst at Enhrenkrantz King Nussbaum, said investors were still pouring money into stock mutual funds.

"People are still thowing money in, whether through 401ks or through money managers," he said, noting that the Investment Company Institute on Wednesday estimated that August inflows to stock mutual funds totalled $19 billion.
"The fundamentals are there. Third-quarter earnings would appear to be a lot better than expected. Higher earnings absent inflation usually mean higher stock prices," LeFevre said.
Many technology stocks powered ahead, bolstered by SoundView Financial's upgrade of the sector.

International Business Machines Corp. rallied 4-7/8 to 122-1/8. Merrill Lynch upgraded IBM, citing its recent unveiling of new products, which may fuel strong earnings in the third and fourth quarters for the computer giant.
Oracle Corp. reported stronger quarterly results and it rose 4-5/8 to 42-1/8. Intel was up 2-3/4 to 88-1/8 and Hewlett-Packard added two to 46-1/2.
Microsoft, which rose 3-1/2 Thursday, added another 2-3/8 to 131, and Motorola bounced back 7/8 to 48-5/8 after falling this week on its earnings warning.
Interest rate-sensitive stocks were bolstered by the drop in the Treasury's bond yield. Fannie Mae rose one to 34-5/8, Merrill Lynch added 1-1/8 to 64-1/4, Citicorp was up 2-1/4 to 88-1/2.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 9.41 to 680.54, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index was 3.60 to 570.26.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.97 to 363.70. The average share was up 42 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,671.108, up 84.746, or 1.29 percent.
